title: Plan and manage time in the workplace

lessons.title: Knowing your time and your tasks
lessons.html:
Why time matters on a farm

On a farm, many jobs must happen at the right time. Cows must be milked on time. Irrigation must start and stop on time. Fruit must be picked before it gets too ripe. If one person is late, others have to wait. The work costs more and the crop or animals can suffer.

Know your working day

  • Know your start time, tea time, lunch time and end time.
  • Arrive a few minutes early so you are ready to start.
  • Know who your supervisor is and where to find them.
  • Know how long it takes to walk or ride from the yard to the block or camp where you work.

Know your tasks

Each day your supervisor gives you tasks. Make sure you understand:

  1. What must be done.
  2. Where it must be done.
  3. By when it must be finished.
  4. What tools or materials you need.

If anything is not clear, ask before you start. A wrong job done fast still wastes time.

Things that waste time

  • Coming late or leaving the work place without telling anyone.
  • Going back to the store because you forgot a tool.
  • Long talks on the phone during work time.
  • Waiting without asking what to do next.
  • Doing work again because it was done badly the first time.

Example

Thandi must fix a fence in camp 4. She checks she has wire, pliers, droppers and gloves before she leaves the yard. She saves an hour because she does not have to walk back for the pliers.

lessons.title: Planning your work and keeping to time
lessons.html:
Making a simple plan

A plan is a list of what you will do and in what order. You can keep it in your head for a small job, but for a full day it helps to write it down or ask your supervisor to go through it with you.

Put the most important things first

Some tasks are more urgent than others. Ask yourself:

  • Will animals or crops suffer if this is late? Do it first. For example, giving water to animals comes before sweeping the shed.
  • Is someone waiting for this job before they can start theirs? Do it early.
  • Can this job wait until tomorrow without harm? Do it later.
TaskWhen
Check water troughs in the campsFirst, in the morning
Load feed bags onto the bakkie for the driverBefore 9:00, the driver is waiting
Clean the tool storeAfter lunch, if time allows

Keep to your plan

  • Get your tools and materials ready before you start.
  • Work steadily. Rest at the set breaks.
  • Check the time now and then. Are you on track?
  • Finish one job properly before starting the next.

When things change

On a farm, plans change. Rain may stop a job, a tractor may break or the supervisor may give you an urgent task. Then:

  1. Tell your supervisor what has changed.
  2. Ask which task is now most important.
  3. Change your plan and carry on.

If you cannot finish a task on time, tell your supervisor early, not at the end of the day.

Key points

  • Know your working hours and arrive ready to start.
  • Understand what, where, by when and with which tools before you start.
  • Do the most urgent and important tasks first.
  • Prepare tools first so you do not waste trips.
  • Tell your supervisor early if plans change or you will be late.

Who else is getting paid more

options.text: Getting tools ready before leaving the yard
Asking when a job is unclear
Going back to the store for a forgotten tool

options.text: At the end of the day
Early, as soon as you know

Sit and wait until the rain stops
